breaks.why: East Asian multibyte charsets (Shift_JIS, BIG5, BIG5-HKSCS, GB2312, EUC-JP): PHP validates their byte sequences and returns an empty string for an invalid one; the port treats them as single-byte and escapes the bytes it is given. The output is still safe: none of < > & " ' can be a trail byte in these sets. WordPress sites on these charsets are rare; see the design spec's breaks ledger.

PCRE resource limits. PHP runs preg_* with pcre.backtrack_limit = 1000000; the bundled PCRE2 the port uses (pcre2 0.2, which exposes no match limit) allows more. On pathological input a WordPress pattern can exhaust PHP's limit and make preg_match return false, which WordPress then treats as no match, while the port still matches. Here force_balance_tags' tag pattern on 'x y': PHP stops balancing ('…y'), the port closes too ('…y'). At 17 and below both match; at 21 and above both give up. Only crafted input reaches the window; the spec's breaks ledger names this class.

Not recorded (it needs a translation filter). When a locale translates the closing curly quote to '', PHP 8's substr_count() in wptexturize_primes() throws ValueError; the port counts no closing quotes and texturizes. Pinned by the PCRE and hand paths alike.

Not recorded (it needs a filter). When a no_texturize_tags or no_texturize_shortcodes filter returns a non-array, PHP 8's in_array() throws TypeError at the first tag or shortcode; the port reads the value as an empty list and texturizes. Pinned in tests/api.rs no_texturize_tags_odd_values.

Not recorded (it needs a filter or a non-string argument). A wp_spaces_regexp fragment that doesn't compile makes PHP warn and its preg_* return null, turning texturized chunks into ''; the port's TextApi returns a TextError instead. A non-scalar wptexturize argument makes PHP throw or warn; the port returns the value unchanged.

PCRE resource limits (see balance_backtrack_18). esc_xml's CDATA regex (a lookahead '(?=.*?<!\[CDATA\[.*?\]\]>)' and lazy groups) exhausts PHP's pcre.backtrack_limit on input such as 471 unterminated '<![CDATA[' (4 KB), and also on any input of about 1 MB or more; preg_replace_callback then returns null and esc_xml returns ''. The port splits CDATA sections with a linear scan and returns the escaped text, which is safe and is what the function means. The spec's 'reproduce WordPress's fallback' would be '' here; the port keeps the escaped output instead (ledger ruling).

wordpress_tests.why: The test writes the $wp_current_filter global to pretend the_title is running. With the native Hook API the filter stack lives in Rust, so writing that global does not change current_filter() and capital_P_dangit() sees no title filter. Its other assertions are in the recorded corpus, and speedyspec_capital_P_dangit_in_filter checks the title case through a real filter.

The test uses PHPUnit's expectError()/expectErrorMessage(), which PHPUnit 10 removed; the pinned PHPUnit is 11. The behaviour it checks (an empty string and a wp_trigger_error() warning for a non-string argument) is in the recorded corpus with its diagnostics, which the natives replay.

engine_behaviour.why: Where a stock body hands null to an internal string function (trailingslashit(null) and untrailingslashit(null) through rtrim, wp_basename(null) through urlencode, normalize_whitespace(null) through trim, backslashit(null) through preg_replace, and the like), PHP raises E_DEPRECATED. The natives read null as '' and raise nothing; the results are the same.

engine_behaviour.what: TypeError for an array passed where a stock body calls an internal string function
engine_behaviour.why: trailingslashit([]), esc_url([]), normalize_whitespace([]), htmlentities2([]) and similar throw TypeError in PHP 8 from the internal function inside the stock body. The natives cast the array as PHP's (string) does ('Array', with PHP's 'Array to string conversion' warning) and return a result. Code that would stop with a fatal error carries on with the 'Array' text.

The natives take their arguments by position only; a named argument (esc_html(text: $x), sanitize_title($t, context: 'query')) is not mapped to its parameter. WordPress does not support named arguments to its functions (its parameter names may change between releases), so callers use positions.

engine_behaviour.what: did_filter('mime_types') while nothing is hooked to it
engine_behaviour.why: sanitize_file_name() reads wp_get_mime_types() from PHP once per request while nothing is hooked to mime_types, so did_filter('mime_types') counts fewer calls than stock. With a callback on the filter, every call goes to PHP and the count matches.

engine_behaviour.what: No PHP frame for formatting callbacks added by name
engine_behaviour.why: add_filter() with one of formatting's functions by name ('wpautop', 'wptexturize', 'esc_url', and the rest WordPress adds in default-filters.php) stores a Rust callback in the same slot, with the same id and the same string in $wp_filter, and runs the native's body without a PHP call. So debug_backtrace() inside a filter that body fires (run_wptexturize, clean_url, ...) has no wpautop()/call_user_func frame, and a runtime override of the function (uopz, runkit) is not seen by callbacks added after the text area loads. Results, order, has_filter() and remove_filter() are unchanged.
